Hi Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo and the clear overview today — appreciate the depth on caching and cost controls. A few follow-up items from our security and engineering teams so we can progress the procurement path:

1) RBAC and least-privilege model: can you share the level of role granularity (org vs project vs dataset), and whether attribute-based access (tags/labels) is supported for policy scoping? We need to map to our internal roles.

2) Support access / break-glass: we need a formal process for vendor support to access customer environments (time-bound, approval workflow, SSO-based auth). Important that all sessions are auditable — who accessed what, and for how long.

3) Audit / logging controls: what events are logged (admin changes, API calls, support sessions), retention period, and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM (Splunk).

4) Data residency / PII: confirmation that customer data can be pinned to us-east1 and any notes on PII handling (masking/transformations) when using hosted API or dedicated deployment.

I've attached our security questionnaire (FinTrust_Security_Questions.xlsx) — the security team filled in the first pass in the "Access Controls" tab and flagged the RBAC and support-access items as high priority.

Next steps: would like to have a short call with product/security folks to walk the RBAC diagram and the break-glass workflow. Are you available next week? Prefer Wed or Thu morning PT.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi Jordan — great to connect yesterday, and thanks for sending the questionnaire.  I pulled in Rishi from our security and product teams to make sure we capture everything.

Quick answers and attachments below; happy to walk through in a 30-min technical review next week:

RBAC / least privilege:
- Redwood supports role-based roles (Org Admin, Project Admin, Engineer, Viewer) and fine-grained project/dataset scoping.
- We also support attribute-based policy tags (env:prod/staging, customer:fintrust) that can be combined with role rules for least-privilege constructs.
- We can provide a sample mapping doc for FinTrust roles.

Support access / break-glass:
- Support engineers may request time-bound access via an approval workflow (customer can require 2nd approver).
- Access uses SSO-backed short-lived credentials (OIDC) and is fully session-audited.
- All support sessions require a justification, ticket link (Jira/HubSpot), and are recorded in our audit logs.
- Break-glass events trigger an alert to your security contacts and create an immutable audit trail.

Logging / audit exports:
- Logged events: admin role changes, token creation/revocation, API calls (with request metadata), support session start/stop, and model inference metadata (no raw PII unless sent in request).
- Default retention on hosted plan: 90 days; enterprise options for 1/3/7 years available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via secure syslog/HTTPS forwarder (we have a Splunk HEC integration).

Data residency / PII:
- We can pin customer data and inference workloads to specific regions (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) on Dedicated and Private; hosted customers can request region pinning as part of enterprise setup.
- PII handling: we recommend application-side masking as the primary control; we offer field-level redaction helpers and guidance for tokenization during ingestion.

Attachments: I've attached a short RBAC overview and our break-glass runbook to give your team a concrete starting point.
- redwood_rbac_overview.pdf
- break-glass-process.docx
